summary: The LLM landscape in 2026 is dominated by a handful of frontier families from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with open-weight models from DeepSeek, Meta, Mistral, and Alibaba capturing substantial developer mindshare. Enterprise adoption is increasingly mediated through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, which amplify real-world usage well beyond direct-API numbers. Because several newest-generation model names (e.g., GPT-6, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4) could not be confirmed with verifiable specifications and availability in the research data, this ranking conservatively lists models whose names, availability, and adoption are well-established.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: GPT-4o remains the default workhorse across ChatGPT and the OpenAI API, and is broadly available through Azure OpenAI, giving it the largest combined direct-API and enterprise-aggregator footprint.
models.best_for: General-purpose assistants and multimodal applications at scale

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's mid-tier Sonnet line is the most-used model for coding workflows and is available via AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, driving heavy enterprise adoption.
models.best_for: Software development and agentic coding assistants

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Gemini 2.5 Pro is cited as the 'context window king' and is natively distributed through Google Vertex AI, giving it strong enterprise and developer reach.
strengths: Deep Google Cloud / Vertex AI integration
models.best_for: Long-context document analysis and large-codebase reasoning

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: Flash's very low cost and 1M-token context make it a high-volume choice for developers, and it is distributed through Google Vertex AI for enterprise consumption.

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek R1 is a 671B-parameter MoE reasoning model with open weights, massive HuggingFace download volume, and availability on AWS Bedrock and Azure, making it the most-adopted open reasoning model.

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek V3 is one of the most-downloaded open-weight general models on HuggingFace and is widely self-hosted for its strong price-performance ratio.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: Llama 3.3 70B is among the most-downloaded open-weight models on HuggingFace and is available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx, giving it unmatched aggregator reach among open models.

models.name: o3
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's o3 reasoning model is heavily used for complex coding and analytical tasks and is available through Azure OpenAI, giving it solid enterprise reach.
strengths: Strong on math, science, and coding
models.best_for: Complex multi-step reasoning and difficult coding problems

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: The lightweight Haiku tier is widely adopted for high-throughput, low-latency tasks and benefits from AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI distribution.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: Qwen3-235B-A22B is a top-downloaded open-weight MoE model on HuggingFace with strong multilingual and coding performance, increasingly used for self-hosted deployments globally.

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Mistral Large 2 is Europe's leading flagship model, available via AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Google Vertex AI, giving it meaningful enterprise adoption within ~25% of the #10 model.
